title: From Language to Drives: A Multimodal Framework for Aligning Autonomous Robots with Human Purposes
abstract: arXiv:2610.35629v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This work explores a multimodal approach to the alignment of the behavior of open-ended learning autonomous robots with human purposes through the use of large language models as cultural enablers. While autonomous robots can generate their own skills and goals through interaction with the environment, they often lack mechanisms to ensure that these remain relevant and aligned to those of human users. The proposed approach makes use of the general and cultural knowledge contained in LLMs and VLMs to establish a multimodal interactive alignment process in which human purposes, expressed in natural language, are transformed into motivational components of a robot architecture in the form of robot missions and drives that guide the behavior of the robot. translated_title: 从语言到驱动力：一个将自主机器人与人类目的对齐的多模态框架
translated_abstract: 这项工作探索了一种多模态方法，通过使用大型语言模型作为文化使能者，将开放式学习自主机器人的行为与人类目的对齐。虽然自主机器人可以通过与环境的交互生成自己的技能和目标，但它们通常缺乏确保这些技能和目标保持相关性并与人类用户目的一致的机制。所提出的方法利用大型语言模型（LLM）和视觉语言模型（VLM）中包含的通用知识和文化知识，建立一个多模态交互式对齐过程，在该过程中，以自然语言表达的人类目的被转换为机器人架构中的动机组件，其形式为指导机器人行为的机器人任务和驱动力。该系统分为三个层次：语义对齐、任务生成和驱动力建模。这种设计实现了一个双向交互循环：人类输入定义高层目标（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个多模态框架，利用大型语言模型和视觉语言模型将人类以自然语言表达的目的转化为机器人的任务和驱动力，从而通过语义对齐、任务生成和驱动力建模三层结构实现自主机器人行为与人类目的的持续对齐。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a multimodal framework that leverages large language models and vision-language models to translate human purposes expressed in natural language into robot missions and drives, achieving continuous alignment of autonomous robots' behavior with human purposes through a three-layer architecture of semantic alignment, mission generation, and drive modeling.
